introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0520 COMMERCE 1, JUNE 2025, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces in the question booklet.

Clés raisonnées mais discutables, à relire par un enseignant de Commerce : 2 (« issue of shares » retenu par élimination, une société de personnes n'émet pas d'actions), 4 (selling in small quantities est un service au détaillant), 9 (« healthy » n'est pas un droit du consommateur tel que formulé), 12 (assessor intervient après le sinistre), 13 (merchantable quality), 17 (consommateur retenu comme dernier maillon ; le détaillant serait la clé si « personne » vise le dernier intermédiaire), 21 (deposit account, le sight deposit account étant assimilé au compte courant), 22 (manufacturing retenu, industry est plus large), 27 (pay-in slip, le relevé de compte étant la réponse concurrente), 28 (le receveur paie la franchise postale), 34 (trade n'est qu'une partie du commerce), 42 (exchange rate retenu ; export subsidies est parfois classé parmi les mesures protectionnistes), 50 (seule option qui est un avantage).

Fautes d'impression du sujet conservées : « Plough back » et « Direct services » sans point, « the buyer owns the goods after payment of;: » (question 15), « pondage » pour postage (question 39), numéros 42 et 43 sans point, « sell goods » (question 38), « Possess » sans s aux options 23 A et D, « installment ». À la question 10, l'option D (« Policy holder. ») est imprimée sans sa lettre ; elle est lue comme D.

Thème de la question 17 : « chain of distribution » plutôt que « channels of distribution », ce dernier nom étant déjà porté par des sujets d'Economics (collision de Tag.name) alors que d'autres sujets de Commerce l'utilisent : à harmoniser au moment de l'ingestion.

Tous les calculs (questions 14, 25, 45) ont été recalculés avec Python. Question 25 : margin = 20 % du prix de vente (clé c) ; 25 % est le taux de marque sur le coût (mark-up), piège a. Question 45 : balance courante = visible + invisible = 1 000 millions de CFAF.

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 33, 37, 43. 33 : loss leaders (clé visée a) est typique des supermarchés, mais accept unwanted goods est aussi discutable. 37 : « open indent » (d) et « general indent » (c) désignent le même document. 43 : shipping note (d) et consignment note (c) sont toutes deux défendables.

questions.enonce_markdown: Losses of public corporations are borne by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A public corporation (a state-owned enterprise such as a national transport, water or electricity company) is owned by the government on behalf of the people. It is financed from public funds, so when it makes a loss the State covers it with money collected from taxes. Partners bear the losses of a partnership, shareholders those of a joint stock company (up to the value of their shares), and the board of directors only manages the enterprise; none of them owns a public corporation.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An external source of finance to a partnership business is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Finance is internal when it comes from inside the business and external when it comes from outside it. Past savings of the partners, ploughed-back profit (profit kept in the business) and money set aside as a provision for taxes are all internal sources. Of the four options, only the issue of shares brings in money from outside investors, so it is the only external source listed.

Note for students: in practice a partnership does not issue shares to the public (that is a feature of a company); its usual external sources are bank loans, overdrafts, trade credit and the admission of a new partner. The question is answered by elimination.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An undercharged invoice is corrected using:
questions.corrige_markdown:
If the seller has charged too little on an invoice (for example by a calculation error), the buyer owes more money. The seller sends a **debit note**, which increases the amount the buyer owes. A credit note does the opposite: it is issued when the buyer was overcharged or returns goods, and it reduces the amount owed. A delivery note only lists goods delivered, and a consignment note accompanies goods being carried.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are services performed by a wholesaler to manufacturers EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A wholesaler serves the manufacturer by buying in bulk (so the manufacturer can produce in large quantities and sell quickly), paying promptly (which helps the manufacturer's cash flow) and advertising or promoting the goods. Selling in small quantities (breaking bulk) is a service the wholesaler gives to **retailers**, not to manufacturers. It is therefore the exception.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A retail firm with many shop locations under one management is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Chain stores (also called multiple shops) are a number of branches in different towns or streets that belong to one firm and are controlled by one head office, often selling the same range of goods at the same prices. A department store is one large shop divided into departments, and supermarkets and hypermarkets are large self-service stores in one place.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Those ships also known as 'taxis' of the sea are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A tramp ship has no fixed route and no fixed timetable: like a taxi, it goes wherever a cargo is available and is hired for that voyage. Liners (coastal or passenger) sail on fixed routes at fixed times, like buses, and tankers are specialised ships for liquid cargo such as oil.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Central banking in Cameroon is carried out by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
BEAC (Banque des Etats de l'Afrique Centrale) is the central bank of Cameroon and the other CEMAC countries: it issues the currency (the CFA franc of Central Africa), keeps the reserves and controls credit. BICEC and SGBC are commercial banks. COBAC is the banking commission that supervises banks; it does not carry out central banking.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Advertising made jointly by manufacturers is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When producers of the same product join together and share the cost of advertising the product as a whole, not one brand (for example, producers of palm oil or milk advertising their product type), it is called **generic** (or collective) advertising. Persuasive advertising tries to convince buyers, informative advertising gives facts about a product, and competitive advertising promotes one brand against rival brands.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are consumers' rights EXCEPT the right to be:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Consumers have the right to be informed (honest labels and prices), the right to consumer education and the right to be represented (heard by consumer associations and in policy making). A person cannot have a right "to be healthy"; the consumer's right is to **safety** and to a healthy environment, and to be protected against goods that harm health. So "Healthy" is the exception.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: After compensation for a loss, the right to scrap value belongs to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Under the principle of **subrogation**, once the insurer has paid full compensation for a loss, it takes over the insured's rights in what remains of the damaged property (the scrap or salvage). The insured must not profit from the loss, which would happen if he or she kept both the compensation and the scrap. The insured and the policy holder are the same person here, and a third party has no rights over the salvage.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The document used when the seller doubts the credit worthiness of a buyer is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A pro forma invoice looks like an invoice but it is not a demand for payment on credit: it tells the buyer the price of the goods and asks for payment **before** the goods are sent. A seller who is unsure that a new buyer will pay later uses it. An ordinary invoice asks for payment after delivery on credit terms, and credit and debit notes only correct earlier invoices.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are used for an insurance policy to be established EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
To set up a policy, the person seeking cover fills in a **proposal form**, an actuary uses statistics of past losses to calculate the risk and the rate of premium, and the **premium** is paid to start the cover. An assessor (loss adjuster) is only called in after a loss has happened to value the damage when a claim is made. He or she is not part of establishing the policy.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Sales of Goods Act states that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Sale of Goods Act sets out terms that are implied in every sale: the seller has the right to sell, the goods must match their description and sample, be fit for their purpose, and be of **merchantable (satisfactory) quality**. Selling under weight is dealt with by weights and measures laws, false descriptions by trade descriptions laws, and showing the cash price clearly by consumer credit rules.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Selling goods below right weight is illegal.
Goods must be of merchantable quality.
Cash price must be shown clearly.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that current assets are 700,000 CFAF and current liabilities are 500,000 CFAF. Working capital is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Working capital = current assets - current liabilities.

Working capital = 700,000 - 500,000 = 200,000 CFAF.

The trap is option B (1,200,000), which adds the two figures instead of subtracting.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a hire purchase transaction, the buyer owns the goods after payment of;:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In hire purchase the buyer takes the goods and uses them at once but pays by instalments. The goods remain the property of the seller (the finance company) until the **last instalment** is paid; only then does ownership pass to the buyer. Until then the seller may take the goods back if the buyer defaults.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Carriage forward as a term of payments means:
questions.corrige_markdown:
"Carriage forward" means that the cost of transporting the goods is not included in the price: the **buyer** pays the carriage when the goods arrive. When the seller pays the transport (the price includes it), the term is "carriage paid".

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Price of goods includes cost of transport.
Buyer is responsible for cost of transport.
Seller is responsible for cost of transport.

questions.enonce_markdown: The last person in the chain of distribution is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The chain of distribution is the route goods follow from the producer to the person who uses them: producer -> wholesaler -> retailer -> **consumer**. The wholesaler, the retailer and the sales agent are intermediaries in the middle of the chain, and the consumer is the final person, who buys the goods to use them.

Note: if "person" is read as "the last trader", the answer would be the retailer; the wording is retained as printed and the consumer is the option that is the end of the chain.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Customs duties are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Customs duties are taxes collected by the customs department on goods that cross the border; the most common ones are **import duties** charged on goods brought into the country. Excise duties are taxes on certain goods made inside the country (such as drinks and tobacco), and "customary duties" is not a trade term. Export duties exist, but they are charged only on some exports, so the standard meaning of customs duties is import duties.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Rate of turnover can be calculated as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The rate of stock turnover shows how many times the average stock is sold and replaced in a period:

Rate of stock turnover = cost of goods sold ÷ average stock.

For example, if the cost of goods sold is 6,000,000 CFAF and the average stock is 1,500,000 CFAF, the stock turns over 4 times a year. The other options mix up the terms and do not measure how fast stock is sold.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Cost of goods sold ÷ average stock.

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of an insurable risk is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A risk can be insured when it is caused by chance, can be measured in money, and the insured has an insurable interest (for example fire, theft, burglary, accident). Gambling and speculation are chosen risks that are taken in the hope of profit, and a change in tastes and fashion is a normal business risk. Insurers do not accept these, so **burglary** is the insurable risk.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An account that earns interest is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **deposit account** (savings account) is meant for keeping money for some time, so the bank pays interest on it. A current account is for daily payments by cheque and normally earns no interest, and a sight deposit account (a deposit that can be withdrawn on demand) is used like a current account. A loan account records money borrowed from the bank, on which the customer pays interest rather than earns it.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The process of change of form of goods is by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Changing the form of materials into a finished or semi-finished product (for example cocoa beans into chocolate, or logs into furniture) is **manufacturing**. Commerce changes the place and time of goods, and direct services give personal help (teaching, medical care).

Industry is the wider branch that also includes extraction and construction; the question asks for the process that specifically changes the form of goods, which is manufacturing.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A business unit is a corporate body when it:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A corporate body (a body corporate) is one that the law recognises as a separate legal person, distinct from its owners. It acquires this status when it is registered and is issued a **certificate of incorporation**. Articles of association are internal rules, a certificate of trading allows a public company to start business, and selling shares to the public is something only public companies may do.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Can sell shares to the public.
Is issued a certificate of trading.

questions.enonce_markdown: The exchange of goods between Cameroon and the US is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trade between two countries only is **bilateral trade**. Multilateral trade involves many countries, and direct trade means trading without intermediaries. "Specific trade" is not a standard trade type.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the cost price of goods is 200,000 CFAF and selling price is 250,000 CFAF, the margin is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Profit = selling price - cost price = 250,000 - 200,000 = 50,000 CFAF.

Margin (as a percentage of the selling price) = profit ÷ selling price x 100 = 50,000 ÷ 250,000 x 100 = **20%**.

The trap is option A: 50,000 ÷ 200,000 x 100 = 25% is the **mark-up** (profit as a percentage of cost price), not the margin.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The transport mode that serves other modes is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Road transport is door-to-door: goods arriving at a seaport, an airport or a railway station are carried on to the buyer by lorry, and goods are brought to the port, the airport or the station by road. Road is therefore the mode that serves (feeds) the other modes.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The document that shows details of money deposited in a bank is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **pay-in slip** (paying-in slip) is filled in when money or cheques are paid into an account. It shows the date, the account, and the notes, coins and cheques deposited, and the customer keeps a counterfoil as proof. A bank statement is a periodic list of all deposits and withdrawals, a standing order form is an instruction to make regular payments, and a cheque is an order to pay money out of an account.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Who pays Free Post services?
questions.corrige_markdown:
With a Free Post (business reply) service, the sender does not stick a stamp on the letter. The post office delivers it and collects the postage from the **receiver**, who is the business that agreed to the service and wants customers to reply easily. The sender (customer or buyer) pays nothing.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the groups below are all primary activities?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Primary (extractive) activities take resources directly from nature: farming, fishing, mining and quarrying, and forestry. In option B all three are primary. Commerce and selling are trade activities, and direct services are a tertiary activity, so the other options each contain an item that is not primary.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The reward to a man-made factor is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A man-made factor is capital (machines, tools, buildings, money used to produce), which is produced by people. The reward for capital is **interest**. Wages reward labour, rent rewards land (a natural resource) and profit rewards the entrepreneur.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The document showing the internal regulations of a company is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **Articles of Association** contain the rules for running the company inside: the rights of shareholders, the powers of directors, how meetings are held and how dividends are paid. The Memorandum of Association governs the relationship of the company with the outside world (name, objects, capital). A prospectus invites the public to buy shares, and a certificate of trading allows a public company to start business.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Impulse buying means:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Impulse buying is buying something that the customer had not planned to buy, usually because of a display, a special offer or a sudden desire. It is not about cheap goods or loss leaders, and it is the opposite of taking time to decide.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is NOT a feature of a department store?

*Options as printed:* A) Sells loss leaders.   B) Accept unwanted goods.   C) Offer free parking to customers.   D) Offer snacks services.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A department store is one large shop divided into departments, each selling a different range of goods. Customers are offered many services: a restaurant or snack bar, free parking, delivery and credit, and many stores take back unwanted goods or change them. Selling loss leaders (goods sold below cost to draw people into the shop) is a technique of supermarkets and hypermarkets, so it is the option that does not describe a department store.

**Intended answer: A (Sells loss leaders).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is NOT a branch of production?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The branches of production are **industry** (extractive, manufacturing and construction), **commerce** (trade and the aids to trade) and **direct services**. Trade is only a part of commerce (the buying and selling), not a branch by itself, so it is the exception.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two lines drawn on the face of a cheque means that payments:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two parallel lines across the face of a cheque make it a **crossed cheque**. The bank will not pay cash over the counter; the money must be paid into a bank account, which protects the drawer if the cheque is lost or stolen. Naming a particular bank in the crossing would restrict payment to that bank, and a cheque does not guarantee payment.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Can be made at a specific branch.
Is made only into an account.

questions.enonce_markdown: A document that records the inventory of a shop is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **bin card** is kept at the place where goods are stored and records the goods received, issued and the balance left in stock, so it records the inventory. A statement of account lists transactions with a customer or supplier, an invoice is a bill for goods sold, and a purchase requisition is a request to the buying department to order goods.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
An order sent to an agent abroad to buy from any manufacturer is known as:

*Options as printed:* A) Closed indent.   B) Indent.   C) General indent.   D) Open indent.
questions.corrige_markdown:
An indent is an order sent by an importer to an agent (indent house) abroad to buy goods on his behalf. In a **closed indent** the importer names the manufacturer to buy from. In an **open indent** (also called a general indent) the agent is free to choose the supplier, "any manufacturer". The intended answer is the open indent, but "general indent" (option C) is another name for the same document in many books, so the printed options do not give a single answer.

**Intended answer: D (Open indent).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A retail organisation that sell goods through the post office using catalogues is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A mail order firm advertises its goods in catalogues and sells by post: the customer chooses from the catalogue, orders and pays by mail, and the goods are delivered by post or by carrier. Supermarkets, hypermarkets and multiple shops all sell through shops that customers visit.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A machine used to stamp pondage on mails is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **franking machine** prints the postage on letters instead of stamps ("pondage" in the question is a misprint for postage) and records the amount used; the business pays the post office in advance for the postage. Fax, telex and telefax machines transmit documents or messages by telecommunication lines.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The document which shows evidence of contract to transport goods by sea is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **bill of lading** is issued by the shipping company when goods are loaded on a ship. It is a receipt for the goods, evidence of the contract of carriage by sea, and a document of title to the goods. A bill of exchange is an order to pay money, and a way bill and a consignment note are used for goods carried by road, rail or air.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A marine insurance policy that covers vessels and their equipment is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In marine insurance, the **hull** policy covers the body of the ship and its equipment (engines, fittings). Cargo insurance covers the goods carried, freight insurance covers the shipowner's loss of freight income, and ship-owners' liability covers claims against the owner for damage caused to others.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are trade restrictions EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trade restrictions are measures a government uses to limit or control foreign trade: an **embargo** (a ban on trade with a country or on certain goods), **quotas** (a limit on the quantity that may be imported), tariffs and exchange controls; subsidies are also listed as protective measures because they help home producers against foreign competitors. The **exchange rate** is simply the price of one currency in terms of another and is not itself a trade restriction.

Note: export subsidies are often treated as a support to exporters, so some books would not count them as a restriction; the exchange rate is the one option that is never a restriction.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A document sent to a shipping agent by the exporter containing instructions for the transportation of goods is;

*Options as printed:* A) Manifest.   B) Delivery note.   C) Consignment note   D) Shipping note
questions.corrige_markdown:
The exporter sends a document to the shipping agent or the port authority with the details of the goods to be shipped and instructions on how they are to be carried. This is usually the **shipping note**. A manifest is a list of all the cargo on a ship prepared by the ship's captain, and a delivery note accompanies goods delivered to a buyer. A consignment note is the document sent with goods to a carrier (road, rail or air) and could also be argued for, so the printed options are not clear enough for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: D (Shipping note).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: In a cheque transaction, the bank is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The three parties to a cheque are the **drawer** (the account holder who writes the cheque), the **payee** (the person to be paid) and the **drawee** (the bank on which the cheque is drawn, which is ordered to pay). So the bank is the drawee.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that visible balance is 800 million CFAF and invisible balance is 200 million CFAF, then current account balance is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The current account balance is the sum of the balance of visible trade (goods) and the balance of invisible trade (services and income).

Current account balance = 800 + 200 = 1,000 million CFAF.

Option C (800 - 200 = 600) wrongly subtracts, and option A doubles the visible balance.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a form of loan to a company?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **debenture** is a certificate for a loan made to a company. The debenture holder is a creditor, not an owner, and receives a fixed rate of interest whether or not the company makes a profit. Ordinary and preference shares (cumulative or not) are part of the share capital, so their holders are owners and receive dividends from profits.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The difference between an overdraft and a loan is that an overdraft:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An overdraft is a facility by which a bank allows a customer to draw more than the balance in the **current account** (the account with a cheque book), up to an agreed limit, and interest is charged only on the amount overdrawn. A loan is a fixed sum paid out for a fixed period, with interest on the whole amount. Both involve interest paid to the bank, so options A and C do not distinguish them, and an overdraft is not granted on savings accounts.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Is granted to savings account holders.
Is granted to current account holders.

questions.enonce_markdown: Turnover in a business is the same as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Turnover is the total value of sales made in a period, after deducting returns (net sales). "Turnover less cost of goods sold" is gross profit, and the other options are not turnover at all, so the answer is total net sales.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Turnover less cost of goods sold.
Cost of goods sold less average stock.

questions.enonce_markdown: Total assets less current liabilities is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Capital employed = total assets - current liabilities (it is the money invested in the business for the long term, equal to the owners' capital plus long-term loans). Working capital is current assets minus current liabilities, and circulating capital is another name for current assets.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an advantage of large-scale retailing?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Large-scale retailers (supermarkets, chain stores) buy in bulk and use self-service, so their personnel cost per unit sold is lower. High overhead costs, high pilfering (theft) and low customer satisfaction are disadvantages, so the only advantage in the list is the decline in the cost of personnel.

**Answer: A.**
